title: PostgreSQL Replication and Backup
summary: Applications connect through a pooler to the primary; WAL streams to a replica and is archived to object storage for point-in-time recovery.

nodes.label: Application
nodes.detail: Opens many short-lived connections and issues queries.

nodes.label: Connection Pool
nodes.detail: Multiplexes many client connections onto a small set of server connections, reducing per-connection memory overhead.

nodes.label: Primary
nodes.detail: Accepts writes. Changes are written to the WAL before the data files, which gives crash safety.

nodes.label: WAL
nodes.detail: Sequential log of every change. It underpins crash recovery, replication and point-in-time recovery.

nodes.label: Streaming Replica
nodes.detail: Receives WAL continuously and replays it. Serves read-only queries and can be promoted on failure.

nodes.label: WAL Archive
nodes.detail: archive_command or a backup tool copies completed WAL segments to external storage.

nodes.label: Object Storage
nodes.detail: Holds base backups and archived WAL, kept off the database hosts.

nodes.label: Restore / PITR
nodes.detail: Restore a base backup, then replay archived WAL up to a chosen timestamp.

steps.title: Pooler fronts the database
steps.text: Clients connect to the pooler, which hands queries to a small number of server connections.

steps.title: Writes hit the WAL first
steps.text: The primary records each change in the WAL before flushing data files.

steps.title: Replica streams WAL
steps.text: The standby receives the WAL stream and replays it, staying close behind the primary.

steps.title: WAL is archived
steps.text: Completed segments plus periodic base backups are uploaded to object storage.

steps.title: Recover to a point in time
steps.text: A base backup is restored and WAL is replayed to the chosen moment.
